simple.meaning: טִירָה (ṭîyrâh) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “a wall ; hence, a fortress or a hamlet.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.

timeline.evidenceText: These are the sons of Ishmael, and these are their names, by their villages, and by their encampments: twelve princes, according to their nations.
All their cities in the places in which they lived, and all their encampments, they burned with fire.
His brother Asaph, who stood on his right hand, even Asaph the son of Berechiah, the son of Shimea,
For they persecute him whom you have wounded.

therefore, behold, I will deliver you to the children of the east for a possession. They will set their encampments in you, and make their dwellings in you. They will eat your fruit and they will drink your milk.
There was a wall around in them, around the four, and boiling places were made under the walls all around.

definitions.full: H2918. tirah [ טִירָה ] noun feminine encampment, battlement (from idea of surrounding , enclosure; Syriac sheepfold , ἔπαυλις ) — construct טִירַת Song 8:9 ; טִירָתָם Psa 69:25 ; plural טִירוֺת Ezek 46:23 ; suffix טִירֹתָם Num 31:10 ; Gen 25:16 ; טִירוֺתָם 1Chr 6:39 ; טִירוֺתֵיהֶם Ezek 25:4 ; — 1 encampment , especially of circular encampment of nomad tribes, mentioned with חצר Gen 25:16 ; with ערים Num 31:10 ; Ezek 25:4 (|| מִשׁכניהם ); encampment (poetry) = habitation Psa 69:26 (|| אהליהם ); more Generally, 1Chr 6:39 (|| מושׁבות ). 2 in metaphor ׳ט כָּ֑סֶף Song 8:9 a battlement of silver. 3 row of stones, only plural טִירוֺת Ezek 46:23 , virtually plural of טוּר 1 , q. v.
